name: Adenocarcinoma of the Small Intestine

ethnicAssociations: Increased risk in Ashkenazi Jewish population

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Small Intestine Adenocarcinoma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of adenocarcinoma in small intestine biopsy or surgical specimen
Radiological evidence of mass lesion or wall thickening in the small intestine on CT or MRI
Presence of obstructive gastrointestinal symptoms or unexplained gastrointestinal bleeding

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma in small intestine tissue with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Endoscopic biopsy may be challenging due to location; surgical resection specimens often required for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive small bowel symptoms (e.g., intermittent bowel obstruction)
pathognomonic.notes: Common presenting symptom due to tumor growth causing luminal narrowing
May present as occult bleeding or overt melena

common.notes: Often crampy or colicky in nature

common.symptomName: Weight loss due to malabsorption or anorexia
searchTerms: weight loss due to appetite loss

common.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

occasional.notes: May be detected on physical examination in advanced cases
May occur due to partial malabsorption
May reflect tumor necrosis or secondary infection
Rare, may occur if tumor invades biliary structures

rare.symptomName: Intussusception caused by tumor acting as a lead point
searchTerms: intestinal blockage from tumor lead point

rare.notes: Very rare, due to ectopic PTHrP production

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as ascites or pleural effusion
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen or chest
ascites or pleural fluid from metastasis

laboratory: Iron-deficiency anemia on complete blood count
Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) in some cases
imaging: CT scan showing irregular mass or wall thickening in small intestine
Endoscopic ultrasound may assist in local staging
genetic: Mutations in KRAS, TP53, and APC genes reported
Association with hereditary cancer syndromes such as Lynch syndrome
other: Histopathology revealing gland-forming malignant epithelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CK20 and CDX2

distinguishingFeatures: Neuroendocrine tumor markers positive (chromogranin A, synaptophysin)
Typically slow growing with hormone-related symptoms
Different histological appearance with nested growth pattern

redFlags: Palpable abdominal mass with weight loss
references: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma, 2024
Orphanet: Adenocarcinoma of the Small Intestine (ORPHA:104075)
UpToDate: Small Intestine Adenocarcinoma: Epidemiology, Clinical Features, and Diagnosis
